newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Zaire spoils Colombian president's S.Africa trip.
newsitem.headline: Zaire spoils Colombian president's S.Africa trip.

text.p: Colombian President Ernesto Samper Pizano left South Africa on Saturday without meeting his host, President Nelson Mandela, who was cooling his heels on board a naval ship awaiting Zaire's warring leaders.

Mandela, usually extremely hospitable and proper in observance of protocol, was forced to abandon discussions with Samper originally planned for Friday and then rescheduled to Saturday morning when the Zairean crisis took precedence.
In a last-ditch attempt to salvage Samper's visit, Mandela invited the Colombian president to join him on the ship later on Saturday morning.
But the two leaders eventually had to settle for telephone conversations, Pretoria foreign affairs official Abdul Minty told a news conference.

"President Mandela invited (Samper) to meet him on the ship today but, unfortunately, due to the schedule of President Samper, it was impossible for him to accept this invitation," Minty said in a prepared statement.
Samper, current chairman of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM), a role which South Africa takes on next year, was due in Kenya later in the day for the second leg of his seven-nation African tour.

Zaire's ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko first delayed the start of the internationally-brokered peace talks due to be chaired by Mandela when he boarded ship five hours later than scheduled and only after a ramp was built to drive him up from the quayside.

Then Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila put paid to Mandela's Saturday engagements with a late night announcement from the Angolan capital Luanda on Friday that he would not join negotiations until security was tightened on the ship.
